name: usage-ledger-token-accuracy
title: Fix token-accuracy gaps in the LLM usage ledger execution plan (cache-token four-field model + completeness/attribution)
description: Amend the existing, plan-only document docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md (delivered by B-1477; no source code implements it yet) to correct accuracy defects BEFORE any implementation bakes them in. Scope is documentation/spec only — no source code, no provider adapter, no runtime registry change in this story. Core defect: the ledger's usage model records only inputTokens/outputTokens/totalTokens, but every Anthropic response returns FOUR token counts — input_tokens (the UNCACHED remainder only), output_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, and cache_read_input_tokens. Real processed volume = input + output + cache_creation + cache_read; cache reads cost ~0.1x and cache writes 1.25x (5min)/2x (1h). In Lattice's long agent loops cache tokens are the dominant cost driver, so a two-field model systematically under-counts tokens and makes cost accounting impossible. The JSON example is the de-facto spec, so the example and the record-shape section must both be corrected. Secondary accuracy fixes: drop the derived totalTokens stored field; prefer the provider count_tokens endpoint for estimates; specify call-time story/phase attribution; add a completeness guarantee (single choke-point writer + reconciliation); capture streaming/failure usage; keep raw provider units AND a normalized canonical view; and add a price/pricingRef snapshot so cost is derivable in a pinned layer.
